text: Antlered Gaulish god, named on the Pillar of the Boatmen in Paris, often shown holding a torc. The name is securely attested only once. Linking other antlered figures, such as the one on the Gundestrup Cauldron, to it is a modern identification. Gods & Goddesses

title: Brigid
summary: The exalted one. Irish goddess of poetry, healing and smithcraft, closely linked with St Brigid of Kildare.
text: Irish goddess of poetry, healing and smithcraft, closely linked with St Brigid of Kildare. How far the saint's cult preserves the goddess is debated. Gods & Goddesses

title: The Morrígan
summary: The phantom queen. Irish goddess of war, fate and sovereignty, who appears as a crow over the battlefield.
text: Irish goddess of war, fate and sovereignty, who appears as a crow over the battlefield.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Lugh
summary: Of the long arm. Irish god skilled in every art, who kills his grandfather Balor at the second battle of Mag Tuired. The festival of Lughnasa bears his name.
text: Irish god skilled in every art, who kills his grandfather Balor at the second battle of Mag Tuired. The festival of Lughnasa bears his name.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Perun
summary: The thunderer. Slavic god of thunder. According to the Primary Chronicle, his idol at Kyiv was thrown into the Dnieper when Prince Vladimir converted in 988.
text: Slavic god of thunder. According to the Primary Chronicle, his idol at Kyiv was thrown into the Dnieper when Prince Vladimir converted in 988.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Veles
summary: Lord of cattle and the underworld. Slavic god of livestock, wealth and the underworld, often seen as Perun's adversary.
text: Slavic god of livestock, wealth and the underworld, often seen as Perun's adversary. The myth of a battle between Perun and Veles is a scholarly reconstruction and is debated. Gods & Goddesses

title: Mokosh
summary: The moist mother. The only goddess in the Kyiv pantheon of 980, linked with spinning, women and the moist earth.
text: The only goddess in the Kyiv pantheon of 980, linked with spinning, women and the moist earth.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Saulė
summary: The sun mother. Sun goddess of Lithuanian and Latvian folk songs, who drives across the sky and sinks into the sea each night.
text: Sun goddess of Lithuanian and Latvian folk songs, who drives across the sky and sinks into the sea each night.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Indra
summary: King of the devas. Chief god of the Rig Veda, who wields the thunderbolt (vajra) and slays the serpent Vritra to release the waters.
text: Chief god of the Rig Veda, who wields the thunderbolt (vajra) and slays the serpent Vritra to release the waters.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Agni
summary: The sacred fire. God of fire and of the sacrificial flame, who carries offerings to the gods. Many hymns of the Rig Veda are addressed to him.
text: God of fire and of the sacrificial flame, who carries offerings to the gods. Many hymns of the Rig Veda are addressed to him.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Varuna
summary: Guardian of cosmic law. Vedic god of the waters and of rita, cosmic order, who sees and punishes wrongdoing; later a god of the ocean.
text: Vedic god of the waters and of rita, cosmic order, who sees and punishes wrongdoing; later a god of the ocean.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Shiva
summary: The auspicious one. Great god of destruction and renewal, ascetic and householder, shown with a third eye, a trident and the crescent moon in his hair.
text: Great god of destruction and renewal, ascetic and householder, shown with a third eye, a trident and the crescent moon in his hair.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Vishnu
summary: The preserver. Preserver of the world, who descends in avatars such as Rama and Krishna, shown with four arms holding conch, discus, mace and lotus.
text: Preserver of the world, who descends in avatars such as Rama and Krishna, shown with four arms holding conch, discus, mace and lotus.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Brahma
summary: The creator. Four-faced creator god, born from a lotus rising from Vishnu's navel in later myth. He has very few temples of his own.
text: Four-faced creator god, born from a lotus rising from Vishnu's navel in later myth. He has very few temples of his own.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Durga
summary: The invincible. Warrior form of the Goddess who rides a lion and slays the buffalo demon Mahishasura, as told in the Devi Mahatmya.
text: Warrior form of the Goddess who rides a lion and slays the buffalo demon Mahishasura, as told in the Devi Mahatmya.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Kali
summary: The black one. Fierce goddess of time and death, with a garland of heads, worshipped especially in Bengal and in Tantra.
text: Fierce goddess of time and death, with a garland of heads, worshipped especially in Bengal and in Tantra.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Ganesha
summary: Remover of obstacles. Elephant-headed son of Shiva and Parvati, honoured at the start of any undertaking.
text: Elephant-headed son of Shiva and Parvati, honoured at the start of any undertaking.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Krishna
summary: The dark one. Avatar of Vishnu, cowherd and flute-player of Vrindavan and teacher of the Bhagavad Gita, beloved of the bhakti poets.
text: Avatar of Vishnu, cowherd and flute-player of Vrindavan and teacher of the Bhagavad Gita, beloved of the bhakti poets.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Lakshmi
summary: Goddess of fortune. Goddess of wealth and good fortune, consort of Vishnu, shown seated on a lotus and bathed by elephants.
text: Goddess of wealth and good fortune, consort of Vishnu, shown seated on a lotus and bathed by elephants.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Saraswati
summary: Goddess of learning. Goddess of knowledge, music and speech, first known as a sacred river of the Rig Veda, shown playing the vina.
text: Goddess of knowledge, music and speech, first known as a sacred river of the Rig Veda, shown playing the vina.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Hanuman
summary: The devoted. Monkey hero of the Ramayana and devotee of Rama, who leaps to Lanka and carries back a mountain of healing herbs.
text: Monkey hero of the Ramayana and devotee of Rama, who leaps to Lanka and carries back a mountain of healing herbs.  Heroes & Sages

title: Avalokiteśvara / Guanyin
summary: The compassionate. Bodhisattva of compassion, worshipped in East Asia in female form as Guanyin (Kannon in Japan), and in Tibet held to be embodied in the Dalai Lama.
text: Bodhisattva of compassion, worshipped in East Asia in female form as Guanyin (Kannon in Japan), and in Tibet held to be embodied in the Dalai Lama.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Amitābha
summary: Buddha of Infinite Light. Buddha of the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī, where those who call on his name hope to be reborn.
text: Buddha of the Pure Land of Sukhāvatī, where those who call on his name hope to be reborn.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Tārā
summary: The saviour. Female bodhisattva and Buddha of Tibetan Buddhism who rescues from fear; Green and White Tārā are her best-known forms.
text: Female bodhisattva and Buddha of Tibetan Buddhism who rescues from fear; Green and White Tārā are her best-known forms.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Maitreya
summary: The Buddha to come. The Buddha of the future, now a bodhisattva in the Tuṣita heaven, expected to appear when the teaching has been forgotten.
text: The Buddha of the future, now a bodhisattva in the Tuṣita heaven, expected to appear when the teaching has been forgotten.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Mañjuśrī
summary: Gentle glory. Bodhisattva of wisdom, who wields a flaming sword that cuts through ignorance and holds a book of the Perfection of Wisdom.
text: Bodhisattva of wisdom, who wields a flaming sword that cuts through ignorance and holds a book of the Perfection of Wisdom.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Māra
summary: The tempter. The demon who tried to stop the Buddha's awakening with armies and with his daughters; the Buddha touched the earth to call it as witness.
text: The demon who tried to stop the Buddha's awakening with armies and with his daughters; the Buddha touched the earth to call it as witness.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Padmasambhava
summary: The lotus-born. Indian master said to have subdued the spirits of Tibet and helped found Samye monastery in the eighth century, revered by the Nyingma school as the Second Buddha.
text: Indian master said to have subdued the spirits of Tibet and helped found Samye monastery in the eighth century, revered by the Nyingma school as the Second Buddha. He is mentioned in early sources, but most of his biography is later legend. Heroes & Sages

title: Mahāvīra
summary: The twenty-fourth Jina. Vardhamāna Mahāvīra, the last of the Jain Tīrthaṅkaras ('ford-makers'), who taught non-violence and attained liberation. His emblem is the lion.
text: Vardhamāna Mahāvīra, the last of the Jain Tīrthaṅkaras ('ford-makers'), who taught non-violence and attained liberation. His emblem is the lion.  Heroes & Sages

title: Pārśvanātha
summary: The twenty-third Jina. Jina shown sheltered by the hood of a many-headed serpent.
text: Jina shown sheltered by the hood of a many-headed serpent. He may have been a historical teacher of the ninth or eighth century BCE. That is possible but not proven. Heroes & Sages

title: Di / Shangdi
summary: The Lord on High. High god of the Shang kings, asked about rain, harvest and war on the oracle bones. The Zhou later spoke more of Heaven (Tian).
text: High god of the Shang kings, asked about rain, harvest and war on the oracle bones. The Zhou later spoke more of Heaven (Tian).  Gods & Goddesses

title: The Jade Emperor
summary: Ruler of Heaven. Supreme ruler of the heavenly bureaucracy in Chinese popular religion and Daoism, to whom the Kitchen God reports each New Year.
text: Supreme ruler of the heavenly bureaucracy in Chinese popular religion and Daoism, to whom the Kitchen God reports each New Year.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Laozi
summary: The Old Master. Traditional author of the Daodejing, deified in Daoism as Taishang Laojun.
text: Traditional author of the Daodejing, deified in Daoism as Taishang Laojun. Whether Laozi was a historical person is debated. Heroes & Sages

title: Confucius (Kongzi)
summary: Master Kong. Teacher of ritual and virtue (traditionally 551–479 BCE), honoured in temples across East Asia; his sayings are collected in the Analects.
text: Teacher of ritual and virtue (traditionally 551–479 BCE), honoured in temples across East Asia; his sayings are collected in the Analects.  Heroes & Sages

title: Xiwangmu
summary: Queen Mother of the West. Goddess of the Kunlun mountains and keeper of the peaches of immortality, whose cult swept across northern China in 3 BCE.
text: Goddess of the Kunlun mountains and keeper of the peaches of immortality, whose cult swept across northern China in 3 BCE.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Guan Yu (Guandi)
summary: God of loyalty. General of the Three Kingdoms period (died 220 CE), deified as Guandi, god of war, loyalty and, for merchants, wealth.
text: General of the Three Kingdoms period (died 220 CE), deified as Guandi, god of war, loyalty and, for merchants, wealth.  Heroes & Sages

title: Amaterasu
summary: Shining in heaven. Sun goddess of the Kojiki, who hid in a cave and plunged the world into darkness. The imperial house claims descent from her; her shrine is at Ise.
text: Sun goddess of the Kojiki, who hid in a cave and plunged the world into darkness. The imperial house claims descent from her; her shrine is at Ise.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Susanoo
summary: The impetuous male. Storm god and brother of Amaterasu, expelled from heaven, who slays the eight-headed serpent and finds a sword in its tail.
text: Storm god and brother of Amaterasu, expelled from heaven, who slays the eight-headed serpent and finds a sword in its tail.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Izanagi
summary: He who invites. With Izanami, stirs the ocean with a jewelled spear to make the islands of Japan. Returning from the land of the dead, he washes and gives birth to the sun, moon and storm.
text: With Izanami, stirs the ocean with a jewelled spear to make the islands of Japan. Returning from the land of the dead, he washes and gives birth to the sun, moon and storm.  Primordial Beings

title: Izanami
summary: She who invites. Co-creator of the islands and gods of Japan, who dies giving birth to fire and becomes the ruler of Yomi, the land of the dead.
text: Co-creator of the islands and gods of Japan, who dies giving birth to fire and becomes the ruler of Yomi, the land of the dead.  Primordial Beings

title: Inari
summary: Kami of rice. Kami of rice, fertility and business, whose messengers are foxes. Fushimi Inari Taisha in Kyoto is famous for its thousands of red gates.
text: Kami of rice, fertility and business, whose messengers are foxes. Fushimi Inari Taisha in Kyoto is famous for its thousands of red gates.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Quetzalcoatl
summary: The feathered serpent. Mesoamerican god of wind, learning and the priesthood, worshipped from Teotihuacan to the Aztecs.
text: Mesoamerican god of wind, learning and the priesthood, worshipped from Teotihuacan to the Aztecs. The story that the Aztecs took Cortés for the returning Quetzalcoatl is now widely doubted by historians. Gods & Goddesses

title: Huitzilopochtli
summary: Hummingbird of the south. Aztec god of the sun and war and patron of Tenochtitlan, born fully armed to defeat his sister Coyolxauhqui. He shared the Templo Mayor with Tlaloc.
text: Aztec god of the sun and war and patron of Tenochtitlan, born fully armed to defeat his sister Coyolxauhqui. He shared the Templo Mayor with Tlaloc.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Tlaloc
summary: The rain god. God of rain and storms, shown with goggle eyes and fangs, whose shrine on the Templo Mayor stood beside Huitzilopochtli's.
text: God of rain and storms, shown with goggle eyes and fangs, whose shrine on the Templo Mayor stood beside Huitzilopochtli's.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Tezcatlipoca
summary: Smoking mirror. Powerful, capricious god of night, sorcery and fate, rival of Quetzalcoatl, with a smoking obsidian mirror in place of one foot.
text: Powerful, capricious god of night, sorcery and fate, rival of Quetzalcoatl, with a smoking obsidian mirror in place of one foot.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Coatlicue
summary: Serpent skirt. Earth goddess and mother of Huitzilopochtli. Her colossal statue, found in Mexico City in 1790, has a head made of two serpents.
text: Earth goddess and mother of Huitzilopochtli. Her colossal statue, found in Mexico City in 1790, has a head made of two serpents.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Itzamnaaj
summary: The aged creator. Old creator god of the Maya and patron of writing and of priests.
text: Old creator god of the Maya and patron of writing and of priests.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Chaak
summary: The rain god. God of rain and lightning, who strikes the clouds with his axe. His long-nosed mask is carved on the buildings of Yucatán.
text: God of rain and lightning, who strikes the clouds with his axe. His long-nosed mask is carved on the buildings of Yucatán.  Gods & Goddesses

title: The Hero Twins
summary: Hunahpu and Xbalanque. Twins of the Popol Vuh, who defeat the lords of the underworld, Xibalba, in a ball game and rise as the sun and the moon.
text: Twins of the Popol Vuh, who defeat the lords of the underworld, Xibalba, in a ball game and rise as the sun and the moon.  Heroes & Sages

title: The Maize God
summary: Death and rebirth. Young god whose death and rebirth follow the cycle of the maize; on Classic Maya vessels he rises from the split earth.
text: Young god whose death and rebirth follow the cycle of the maize; on Classic Maya vessels he rises from the split earth.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Viracocha
summary: The creator. Creator god who, in myths written down after the Spanish conquest, rises from Lake Titicaca, makes the sun and moon and walks away across the sea.
text: Creator god who, in myths written down after the Spanish conquest, rises from Lake Titicaca, makes the sun and moon and walks away across the sea. He is often identified with the Staff God of Tiwanaku, which is centuries older than the Inca. That identification is not proven. Gods & Goddesses

title: Inti
summary: The sun. Sun god and divine ancestor of the Inca rulers, worshipped at the Coricancha in Cusco and at the festival of Inti Raymi.
text: Sun god and divine ancestor of the Inca rulers, worshipped at the Coricancha in Cusco and at the festival of Inti Raymi.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Pachamama
summary: Mother earth. The earth mother of Andean peoples, still honoured today with offerings (pagos) of coca, maize beer and food.
text: The earth mother of Andean peoples, still honoured today with offerings (pagos) of coca, maize beer and food.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Mama Quilla
summary: Mother moon. Moon goddess and wife of Inti, who governed the ritual calendar and protected women.
text: Moon goddess and wife of Inti, who governed the ritual calendar and protected women.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Olódùmarè
summary: The supreme being. The distant high god of Yoruba religion, owner of the heavens, approached through the orishas rather than worshipped directly.
text: The distant high god of Yoruba religion, owner of the heavens, approached through the orishas rather than worshipped directly.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Ọbàtálá
summary: King of the white cloth. Orisha who shaped human bodies from clay, associated with purity, calm judgement and the colour white.
text: Orisha who shaped human bodies from clay, associated with purity, calm judgement and the colour white.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Ògún
summary: Lord of iron. Orisha of iron, hunting, war and technology, patron of smiths, drivers and everyone who works with metal.
text: Orisha of iron, hunting, war and technology, patron of smiths, drivers and everyone who works with metal.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Ṣàngó
summary: Lord of thunder. Orisha of thunder and lightning, remembered as a king of Oyo, whose emblem is the double axe.
text: Orisha of thunder and lightning, remembered as a king of Oyo, whose emblem is the double axe.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Ọ̀ṣun
summary: Lady of the river. Orisha of the Osun river, of love, fertility and sweet water, honoured each year at the sacred grove of Osogbo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
text: Orisha of the Osun river, of love, fertility and sweet water, honoured each year at the sacred grove of Osogbo, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Èṣù
summary: Guardian of the crossroads. Messenger between people and the orishas and keeper of the crossroads, who must be honoured first. Missionaries wrongly equated him with the Devil.
text: Messenger between people and the orishas and keeper of the crossroads, who must be honoured first. Missionaries wrongly equated him with the Devil.  Tricksters

title: Yemọja
summary: Mother of waters. Orisha of the Ogun river and, in the Americas as Yemayá, of the ocean; a mother of the orishas.
text: Orisha of the Ogun river and, in the Americas as Yemayá, of the ocean; a mother of the orishas.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Papa Legba
summary: Keeper of the gate. The Vodou lwa who opens the gate between people and the spirits and is saluted first in every ceremony; he is related to Legba and Eshu of West Africa.
text: The Vodou lwa who opens the gate between people and the spirits and is saluted first in every ceremony; he is related to Legba and Eshu of West Africa.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Ezili Freda
summary: Lady of love. Lwa of love, luxury and beauty in Haitian Vodou, often associated with images of the Virgin Mary. Her vèvè is a heart.
text: Lwa of love, luxury and beauty in Haitian Vodou, often associated with images of the Virgin Mary. Her vèvè is a heart.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Baron Samedi
summary: Lord of the cemetery. Head of the Gede, the lwa of death and the dead in Haitian Vodou, dressed in top hat and tails, bawdy, and also a healer.
text: Head of the Gede, the lwa of death and the dead in Haitian Vodou, dressed in top hat and tails, bawdy, and also a healer.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Michael
summary: Who is like God?. Archangel named in Daniel and Revelation as leader of the heavenly army against the dragon; Mīkāl in the Qur'an.
text: Archangel named in Daniel and Revelation as leader of the heavenly army against the dragon; Mīkāl in the Qur'an.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Metatron
summary: Prince of the Presence. Great angel of the Hebrew Book of Enoch (3 Enoch), identified there with the transformed Enoch, and an important figure in Jewish mysticism.
text: Great angel of the Hebrew Book of Enoch (3 Enoch), identified there with the transformed Enoch, and an important figure in Jewish mysticism.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Lilith
summary: The night demoness. A demoness who threatens women and infants in Jewish tradition, named once in Isaiah 34:14 and bound on the Babylonian incantation bowls.
text: A demoness who threatens women and infants in Jewish tradition, named once in Isaiah 34:14 and bound on the Babylonian incantation bowls. The story that she was Adam's first wife comes from the medieval Alphabet of Ben Sira, not from the Bible. Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Asmodeus
summary: King of demons. Demon of the Book of Tobit, who kills seven husbands of Sarah until Raphael drives him away; in the Talmud he is king of demons and serves Solomon.
text: Demon of the Book of Tobit, who kills seven husbands of Sarah until Raphael drives him away; in the Talmud he is king of demons and serves Solomon.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Iblīs
summary: The one who refused. In the Qur'an, the being who refused to bow to Adam and was cast out, becoming the tempter of humankind; he is described as created from fire.
text: In the Qur'an, the being who refused to bow to Adam and was cast out, becoming the tempter of humankind; he is described as created from fire.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: The Jinn
summary: Beings of smokeless fire. Beings created from smokeless fire in the Qur'an, unseen, able to believe or disbelieve, and the subject of a vast folk tradition.
text: Beings created from smokeless fire in the Qur'an, unseen, able to believe or disbelieve, and the subject of a vast folk tradition.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Satan
summary: The adversary. In the Hebrew Bible 'the satan' is an accuser in God's court (Job); later Jewish and Christian writings make him the chief enemy of God. Modern Satanists use him as a symbol of rebellion.
text: In the Hebrew Bible 'the satan' is an accuser in God's court (Job); later Jewish and Christian writings make him the chief enemy of God. Modern Satanists use him as a symbol of rebellion.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Sophia
summary: Wisdom. In many Gnostic texts, the aeon whose attempt to create without her partner brings the flawed world into being; in the Pistis Sophia she repents and is rescued.
text: In many Gnostic texts, the aeon whose attempt to create without her partner brings the flawed world into being; in the Pistis Sophia she repents and is rescued.  Primordial Beings

title: Yaldabaoth
summary: The Demiurge. In Sethian texts such as the Apocryphon of John, the ignorant creator of the material world, born of Sophia as a lion-faced serpent.
text: In Sethian texts such as the Apocryphon of John, the ignorant creator of the material world, born of Sophia as a lion-faced serpent.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Abraxas
summary: The number 365. Name carved on late antique magical gems with a cock-headed, serpent-legged figure. Its Greek letters add up to 365, the days of the year.
text: Name carved on late antique magical gems with a cock-headed, serpent-legged figure. Its Greek letters add up to 365, the days of the year.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Tawûsê Melek
summary: The Peacock Angel. Chief of the seven angels to whom God entrusted the world in Yazidi belief. Outsiders long and wrongly equated him with Satan, which fed persecution.
text: Chief of the seven angels to whom God entrusted the world in Yazidi belief. Outsiders long and wrongly equated him with Satan, which fed persecution.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: The Rainbow Serpent
summary: Maker of waterways. A great serpent linked with water, rain and the shaping of the land in the stories of many Aboriginal peoples, known by many names, such as Ngalyod and Wagyl.
text: A great serpent linked with water, rain and the shaping of the land in the stories of many Aboriginal peoples, known by many names, such as Ngalyod and Wagyl. 'Rainbow Serpent' is a single English label applied by scholars in the twentieth century to many distinct local beings. Primordial Beings

title: Māui
summary: The demigod. Polynesian trickster hero who fishes up islands with his magic hook, snares the sun to slow it and seeks immortality for people.
text: Polynesian trickster hero who fishes up islands with his magic hook, snares the sun to slow it and seeks immortality for people.  Tricksters

title: Pele
summary: Goddess of the volcano. Hawaiian goddess of fire and volcanoes, said to live in the crater of Kīlauea.
text: Hawaiian goddess of fire and volcanoes, said to live in the crater of Kīlauea.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Tangaroa
summary: God of the sea. Great god of the ocean across Polynesia (Tangaloa in Samoa, Kanaloa in Hawaii), in some islands the creator.
text: Great god of the ocean across Polynesia (Tangaloa in Samoa, Kanaloa in Hawaii), in some islands the creator.  Gods & Goddesses

title: Coyote
summary: The trickster. Clever, greedy and foolish trickster, and sometimes creator, in the stories of many peoples of the American West and Southwest.
text: Clever, greedy and foolish trickster, and sometimes creator, in the stories of many peoples of the American West and Southwest.  Tricksters

title: Raven
summary: He who stole the light. Transformer and trickster of the Pacific Northwest (Haida, Tlingit and others), who released the sun, moon and stars from a box.
text: Transformer and trickster of the Pacific Northwest (Haida, Tlingit and others), who released the sun, moon and stars from a box.  Tricksters

title: Sky Woman
summary: She who fell from the sky. In Haudenosaunee creation, the woman who falls from the sky world and lands on the back of a turtle, where the earth is made.
text: In Haudenosaunee creation, the woman who falls from the sky world and lands on the back of a turtle, where the earth is made.  Primordial Beings

title: The Horned God
summary: Lord of the wild. The god of modern Wicca, lord of animals, the hunt and death, partner of the Goddess.
text: The god of modern Wicca, lord of animals, the hunt and death, partner of the Goddess. His form was shaped by Margaret Murray's theory of a surviving pagan witch cult, which historians now reject. Gods & Goddesses

title: The Triple Goddess
summary: Maiden, Mother, Crone. The Goddess of modern Wicca and Paganism in threefold form, popularised by Robert Graves in The White Goddess (1948).
text: The Goddess of modern Wicca and Paganism in threefold form, popularised by Robert Graves in The White Goddess (1948). Ancient triple goddesses existed, but the idea of one universal Triple Goddess is modern. Gods & Goddesses

title: Baphomet
summary: The goat-headed idol. Named in the 1307–1312 trials of the Knights Templar as an idol they supposedly worshipped. The familiar winged, goat-headed image was drawn by Éliphas Lévi in 1856 and later adopted by modern Satanism.
text: Named in the 1307–1312 trials of the Knights Templar as an idol they supposedly worshipped. The familiar winged, goat-headed image was drawn by Éliphas Lévi in 1856 and later adopted by modern Satanism. The Templar confessions were extracted under torture, and historians do not accept that they worshipped any such idol. Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: YHWH, the God of Israel
summary: I am who I am. The God of the Hebrew Bible, whose four-letter name, the Tetragrammaton, Jews do not pronounce, reading 'Adonai', 'the Lord', in its place. Worshipped as the one God in Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Shown here only by the written name, since Jewish tradition forbids images of God.
text: The God of the Hebrew Bible, whose four-letter name, the Tetragrammaton, Jews do not pronounce, reading 'Adonai', 'the Lord', in its place. Worshipped as the one God in Judaism, Christianity and Islam. Shown here only by the written name, since Jewish tradition forbids images of God. How Israel's God emerged from a wider Canaanite world of gods, and when worship of him alone became the rule, is debated by historians. Gods & Goddesses

title: Adam
summary: The first man. Formed from the dust of the ground and placed in the garden of Eden (Genesis 2), then sent out to till the soil. In the Qur'an, Ādam is the first prophet.
text: Formed from the dust of the ground and placed in the garden of Eden (Genesis 2), then sent out to till the soil. In the Qur'an, Ādam is the first prophet.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Eve
summary: Mother of all living. The first woman, who eats the forbidden fruit at the serpent's urging (Genesis 3). Genesis does not name the fruit; the apple comes from later Latin tradition.
text: The first woman, who eats the forbidden fruit at the serpent's urging (Genesis 3). Genesis does not name the fruit; the apple comes from later Latin tradition.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Enoch
summary: He walked with God. Seventh from Adam, who 'walked with God; and he was not, for God took him' (Genesis 5:24). He became the seer of the Books of Enoch, and in later mysticism the angel Metatron.
text: Seventh from Adam, who 'walked with God; and he was not, for God took him' (Genesis 5:24). He became the seer of the Books of Enoch, and in later mysticism the angel Metatron.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Noah
summary: Builder of the ark. Saved with his family and the animals from the flood in Genesis 6–9; God's covenant with him is sealed by the rainbow. Nūḥ is a prophet in the Qur'an.
text: Saved with his family and the animals from the flood in Genesis 6–9; God's covenant with him is sealed by the rainbow. Nūḥ is a prophet in the Qur'an. The story has close parallels in older Mesopotamian flood stories; see The Flood (ch01). Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Abraham
summary: Father of many nations. Patriarch called by God to leave his homeland for Canaan; ancestor of Israel through Isaac and, in tradition, of the Arabs through Ishmael. Ibrāhīm, the 'friend of God', in the Qur'an.
text: Patriarch called by God to leave his homeland for Canaan; ancestor of Israel through Isaac and, in tradition, of the Arabs through Ishmael. Ibrāhīm, the 'friend of God', in the Qur'an. Whether the patriarchs were historical individuals is debated; there is no direct archaeological evidence for them. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Sarah
summary: Mother of Isaac. Wife of Abraham, who laughs at the promise of a son in her old age and then bears Isaac, whose name means 'he laughs'.
text: Wife of Abraham, who laughs at the promise of a son in her old age and then bears Isaac, whose name means 'he laughs'.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Hagar
summary: The one who saw God. Egyptian servant of Sarah and mother of Ishmael, sent into the desert and saved by an angel. Muslims recall her search for water in the running between Safa and Marwa at Mecca.
text: Egyptian servant of Sarah and mother of Ishmael, sent into the desert and saved by an angel. Muslims recall her search for water in the running between Safa and Marwa at Mecca.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Isaac
summary: The bound one. Son of Abraham and Sarah, whom Abraham is commanded to sacrifice and who is spared at the last moment, a ram taking his place (the Akedah, Genesis 22).
text: Son of Abraham and Sarah, whom Abraham is commanded to sacrifice and who is spared at the last moment, a ram taking his place (the Akedah, Genesis 22).  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Ishmael
summary: Ancestor of the Arabs. Son of Abraham and Hagar, who grows up in the wilderness as an archer. In the Qur'an, Ismāʿīl helps his father raise the Kaaba, and many Muslim scholars hold him to be the son Abraham was asked to sacrifice.
text: Son of Abraham and Hagar, who grows up in the wilderness as an archer. In the Qur'an, Ismāʿīl helps his father raise the Kaaba, and many Muslim scholars hold him to be the son Abraham was asked to sacrifice.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Jacob (Israel)
summary: He who strove with God. Son of Isaac, who dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven and wrestles through the night with a divine being, receiving the name Israel. His twelve sons are the ancestors of the tribes.
text: Son of Isaac, who dreams of a ladder reaching to heaven and wrestles through the night with a divine being, receiving the name Israel. His twelve sons are the ancestors of the tribes.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Joseph
summary: The dreamer. Jacob's favourite son, sold into Egypt by his brothers, who rises to rule Egypt by interpreting Pharaoh's dreams of fat and lean years. Yūsuf's story fills a whole sura of the Qur'an.
text: Jacob's favourite son, sold into Egypt by his brothers, who rises to rule Egypt by interpreting Pharaoh's dreams of fat and lean years. Yūsuf's story fills a whole sura of the Qur'an.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Moses
summary: The lawgiver. Leader of the Exodus from Egypt, who receives the Law on Mount Sinai: the greatest of the prophets in Judaism, and Mūsā, the prophet most often named in the Qur'an. The rays of light follow Exodus 34, where his face shines.
text: Leader of the Exodus from Egypt, who receives the Law on Mount Sinai: the greatest of the prophets in Judaism, and Mūsā, the prophet most often named in the Qur'an. The rays of light follow Exodus 34, where his face shines. Archaeologists find no direct evidence for the Exodus as described; how far the story preserves a historical memory is debated. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Aaron
summary: The first high priest. Brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel, ancestor of the priestly line, the kohanim, whose rod blossomed as a sign of his election.
text: Brother of Moses and first high priest of Israel, ancestor of the priestly line, the kohanim, whose rod blossomed as a sign of his election.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Miriam
summary: The prophetess. Sister of Moses and Aaron, who leads the women with a hand-drum in song and dance after the crossing of the sea (Exodus 15).
text: Sister of Moses and Aaron, who leads the women with a hand-drum in song and dance after the crossing of the sea (Exodus 15).  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Joshua
summary: Successor of Moses. Leader who takes Israel across the Jordan into Canaan; at Jericho, the walls fall at the sound of the priests' trumpets.
text: Leader who takes Israel across the Jordan into Canaan; at Jericho, the walls fall at the sound of the priests' trumpets. Archaeology does not support a sudden conquest of Canaan; Jericho appears to have been largely unoccupied at the time usually proposed. Heroes & Sages

title: Deborah
summary: Judge and prophetess. A prophetess who judged Israel under a palm tree and led the victory over Sisera. Her song (Judges 5) is among the oldest poems in the Bible.
text: A prophetess who judged Israel under a palm tree and led the victory over Sisera. Her song (Judges 5) is among the oldest poems in the Bible.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Samson
summary: The strong. Judge of enormous strength whose power lies in his uncut hair, betrayed by Delilah, who brings down the temple of Dagon on the Philistines and himself.
text: Judge of enormous strength whose power lies in his uncut hair, betrayed by Delilah, who brings down the temple of Dagon on the Philistines and himself.  Heroes & Sages

title: Ruth
summary: Your people shall be my people. A Moabite widow who stays with her mother-in-law Naomi, gleans in the fields of Boaz, and becomes the great-grandmother of King David.
text: A Moabite widow who stays with her mother-in-law Naomi, gleans in the fields of Boaz, and becomes the great-grandmother of King David.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Samuel
summary: The kingmaker. The last of the judges, a prophet who anoints first Saul and then David as king of Israel with a horn of oil.
text: The last of the judges, a prophet who anoints first Saul and then David as king of Israel with a horn of oil.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: David
summary: The shepherd king. Shepherd and musician who kills Goliath and becomes king of Israel, with Jerusalem as his capital; the traditional author of many Psalms, and Dāwūd in the Qur'an.
text: Shepherd and musician who kills Goliath and becomes king of Israel, with Jerusalem as his capital; the traditional author of many Psalms, and Dāwūd in the Qur'an. The Tel Dan inscription is widely read as naming the 'House of David', but the size of his kingdom is debated. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Solomon
summary: The wise king. Son of David, famed for wisdom and wealth, builder of the First Temple in Jerusalem. In the Kebra Nagast he fathers Menelik with the Queen of Sheba; as Sulaymān in the Qur'an, he commands the jinn with a seal ring.
text: Son of David, famed for wisdom and wealth, builder of the First Temple in Jerusalem. In the Kebra Nagast he fathers Menelik with the Queen of Sheba; as Sulaymān in the Qur'an, he commands the jinn with a seal ring. No inscription from his reign has been found, and the scale of his kingdom is debated. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: The Queen of Sheba
summary: Queen of the south. Queen who comes to test Solomon's wisdom with riddles and gifts (1 Kings 10); called Makeda in Ethiopia and Bilqīs in Islamic tradition.
text: Queen who comes to test Solomon's wisdom with riddles and gifts (1 Kings 10); called Makeda in Ethiopia and Bilqīs in Islamic tradition. Where Sheba was, in southern Arabia or in Africa, is debated. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Elijah
summary: The prophet of fire. Prophet who calls down fire on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal and is taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire. Jewish tradition awaits his return before the Messiah.
text: Prophet who calls down fire on Mount Carmel against the prophets of Baal and is taken up to heaven in a chariot of fire. Jewish tradition awaits his return before the Messiah.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Jezebel
summary: Queen of Israel. Phoenician princess of Tyre and queen of Israel, patron of the worship of Baal and enemy of Elijah, remembered in the Bible as the model of a wicked queen.
text: Phoenician princess of Tyre and queen of Israel, patron of the worship of Baal and enemy of Elijah, remembered in the Bible as the model of a wicked queen.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Isaiah
summary: Prophet of the Holy One. Eighth-century BCE prophet of Jerusalem whose book foretells a coming king of peace. Christians read many of its passages as prophecies of Christ.
text: Eighth-century BCE prophet of Jerusalem whose book foretells a coming king of peace. Christians read many of its passages as prophecies of Christ. Scholars generally hold that the book of Isaiah combines the work of more than one author and period. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Jeremiah
summary: The weeping prophet. Prophet who warned of Jerusalem's fall to Babylon, wearing a yoke as a sign of submission, and lived through the destruction of 587/586 BCE.
text: Prophet who warned of Jerusalem's fall to Babylon, wearing a yoke as a sign of submission, and lived through the destruction of 587/586 BCE.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Ezekiel
summary: The visionary. Prophet of the Babylonian exile who sees the throne-chariot of God, with its wheels full of eyes, and the valley of dry bones restored to life. His vision became the root of Merkavah mysticism.
text: Prophet of the Babylonian exile who sees the throne-chariot of God, with its wheels full of eyes, and the valley of dry bones restored to life. His vision became the root of Merkavah mysticism.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Daniel
summary: In the lions' den. Judean exile at the Babylonian court, saved from the lions' den, whose visions of beasts and 'one like a son of man' shaped later apocalyptic thought.
text: Judean exile at the Babylonian court, saved from the lions' den, whose visions of beasts and 'one like a son of man' shaped later apocalyptic thought. Most scholars date the book of Daniel to about 165 BCE, in the Maccabean period, rather than the sixth century BCE it describes. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Jonah
summary: Swallowed by the fish. Prophet who flees God's call, is swallowed by a great fish, and preaches repentance to Nineveh. Yūnus in the Qur'an.
text: Prophet who flees God's call, is swallowed by a great fish, and preaches repentance to Nineveh. Yūnus in the Qur'an.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Esther
summary: Queen of Persia. Jewish queen of Persia who saves her people from Haman's plot, a deliverance celebrated at the festival of Purim, when her scroll is read aloud.
text: Jewish queen of Persia who saves her people from Haman's plot, a deliverance celebrated at the festival of Purim, when her scroll is read aloud.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Job
summary: The patient sufferer. A righteous man tested by suffering after 'the satan' questions his piety. The book is one of the great works on why the innocent suffer.
text: A righteous man tested by suffering after 'the satan' questions his piety. The book is one of the great works on why the innocent suffer.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Judah Maccabee
summary: The Hammer. Leader of the Jewish revolt against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV, who retook and rededicated the Temple in 164 BCE, the origin of Hanukkah.
text: Leader of the Jewish revolt against the Seleucid king Antiochus IV, who retook and rededicated the Temple in 164 BCE, the origin of Hanukkah.  Heroes & Sages

title: Judith
summary: Heroine of Bethulia. Widow of the Book of Judith, among the deuterocanonical books, who saves her city by beheading the Assyrian general Holofernes.
text: Widow of the Book of Judith, among the deuterocanonical books, who saves her city by beheading the Assyrian general Holofernes.  Heroes & Sages

title: Gabriel (Jibrīl)
summary: God is my strength. Archangel who explains Daniel's visions, announces the births of John and Jesus in Luke, and, as Jibrīl, brings the Qur'an to Muhammad.
text: Archangel who explains Daniel's visions, announces the births of John and Jesus in Luke, and, as Jibrīl, brings the Qur'an to Muhammad.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Raphael
summary: God heals. Archangel of the Book of Tobit, who guides the young Tobias, drives away the demon Asmodeus, and heals Tobit's blindness with the gall of a fish.
text: Archangel of the Book of Tobit, who guides the young Tobias, drives away the demon Asmodeus, and heals Tobit's blindness with the gall of a fish.  Spirits, Angels & Demons

title: Jesus of Nazareth
summary: The Christ. Jewish teacher and healer of Galilee, crucified in Jerusalem under Pontius Pilate around 30 CE. Christians proclaim him the risen Son of God and the second person of the Trinity; in the Qur'an, ʿĪsā is a prophet and the Messiah, born of the Virgin Mary.
text: Jewish teacher and healer of Galilee, crucified in Jerusalem under Pontius Pilate around 30 CE. Christians proclaim him the risen Son of God and the second person of the Trinity; in the Qur'an, ʿĪsā is a prophet and the Messiah, born of the Virgin Mary. Nearly all historians accept that Jesus lived and was crucified; his divinity and resurrection are matters of faith, and many relics linked with him are of disputed authenticity. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Mary, mother of Jesus
summary: Theotokos. Mother of Jesus, venerated in Catholic and Orthodox Christianity as the Mother of God and Queen of Heaven. Maryam is the only woman named in the Qur'an, where a sura bears her name.
text: Mother of Jesus, venerated in Catholic and Orthodox Christianity as the Mother of God and Queen of Heaven. Maryam is the only woman named in the Qur'an, where a sura bears her name.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: John the Baptist
summary: The forerunner. Ascetic preacher who baptised in the Jordan, Jesus among others, and was beheaded by Herod Antipas. Yaḥyā in the Qur'an, and the great prophet of the Mandaeans.
text: Ascetic preacher who baptised in the Jordan, Jesus among others, and was beheaded by Herod Antipas. Yaḥyā in the Qur'an, and the great prophet of the Mandaeans.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Peter
summary: The rock. Galilean fisherman and leader of the twelve apostles, who denied Jesus three times; by tradition martyred in Rome and the first bishop of Rome, holder of the keys of heaven.
text: Galilean fisherman and leader of the twelve apostles, who denied Jesus three times; by tradition martyred in Rome and the first bishop of Rome, holder of the keys of heaven.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Paul
summary: Apostle to the Gentiles. Pharisee and persecutor of the first Christians who turned apostle after a vision on the road to Damascus. His letters are the earliest surviving Christian writings.
text: Pharisee and persecutor of the first Christians who turned apostle after a vision on the road to Damascus. His letters are the earliest surviving Christian writings. Scholars accept seven of the letters under his name as his own and debate the authorship of the rest. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Mary Magdalene
summary: Apostle to the apostles. Follower of Jesus and, in the Gospels, the first witness of the resurrection. The idea that she was a repentant prostitute comes from a sermon of Pope Gregory I in 591, not from the Bible.
text: Follower of Jesus and, in the Gospels, the first witness of the resurrection. The idea that she was a repentant prostitute comes from a sermon of Pope Gregory I in 591, not from the Bible.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: John the Apostle
summary: The beloved disciple. One of the twelve, traditionally credited with the Fourth Gospel, three letters and the Book of Revelation; his symbol is the eagle.
text: One of the twelve, traditionally credited with the Fourth Gospel, three letters and the Book of Revelation; his symbol is the eagle. Scholars debate whether the apostle wrote any of the works attributed to him. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Thomas
summary: The doubter. Apostle who would not believe in the resurrection until he touched Jesus' wounds; by tradition the apostle of India, and the name on the Gospel of Thomas.
text: Apostle who would not believe in the resurrection until he touched Jesus' wounds; by tradition the apostle of India, and the name on the Gospel of Thomas.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Judas Iscariot
summary: The betrayer. Apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. The Gnostic Gospel of Judas presents him instead as the one disciple who understood Jesus.
text: Apostle who betrayed Jesus for thirty pieces of silver. The Gnostic Gospel of Judas presents him instead as the one disciple who understood Jesus.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: James, brother of Jesus
summary: James the Just. Leader of the church in Jerusalem, called the brother of the Lord, executed in 62 CE according to the historian Josephus.
text: Leader of the church in Jerusalem, called the brother of the Lord, executed in 62 CE according to the historian Josephus.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Pontius Pilate
summary: Prefect of Judaea. Roman prefect of Judaea from about 26 to 36 CE, who condemned Jesus to crucifixion. His name and title appear on an inscription found at Caesarea in 1961.
text: Roman prefect of Judaea from about 26 to 36 CE, who condemned Jesus to crucifixion. His name and title appear on an inscription found at Caesarea in 1961.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Herod the Great
summary: King of Judaea. King of Judaea under Rome (37–4 BCE), who rebuilt the Temple on a vast scale. The Gospel of Matthew makes him the killer of the infants of Bethlehem.
text: King of Judaea under Rome (37–4 BCE), who rebuilt the Temple on a vast scale. The Gospel of Matthew makes him the killer of the infants of Bethlehem. The massacre of the innocents is recorded only in Matthew. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Lazarus
summary: Raised from the dead. Brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany, whom Jesus raises from the tomb after four days (John 11).
text: Brother of Martha and Mary of Bethany, whom Jesus raises from the tomb after four days (John 11).  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Joseph of Arimathea
summary: Keeper of the tomb. Wealthy disciple who laid Jesus' body in his own tomb. Medieval legend brought him to Britain with the Holy Grail.
text: Wealthy disciple who laid Jesus' body in his own tomb. Medieval legend brought him to Britain with the Holy Grail. The Grail and Glastonbury stories are medieval legends. Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Muhammad
summary: The Messenger of God. The Prophet of Islam (c. 570–632 CE), who received the revelations of the Qur'an in Mecca and Medina and founded the first Muslim community. Muslims hold him to be the last of the prophets, the 'Seal of the Prophets'. Following Islamic practice, he is shown only by his name in calligraphy.
text: The Prophet of Islam (c. 570–632 CE), who received the revelations of the Qur'an in Mecca and Medina and founded the first Muslim community. Muslims hold him to be the last of the prophets, the 'Seal of the Prophets'. Following Islamic practice, he is shown only by his name in calligraphy.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Khadija
summary: Mother of the believers. Merchant of Mecca, first wife of Muhammad, and the first person to accept his message.
text: Merchant of Mecca, first wife of Muhammad, and the first person to accept his message.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Fatima
summary: The radiant. Daughter of Muhammad and Khadija, wife of ʿAlī and mother of Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, especially revered in Shiʿi Islam.
text: Daughter of Muhammad and Khadija, wife of ʿAlī and mother of Ḥasan and Ḥusayn, especially revered in Shiʿi Islam.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib
summary: The first Imam. Cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, fourth caliph in Sunni reckoning and first Imam of Shiʿi Islam, assassinated at Kufa in 661.
text: Cousin and son-in-law of Muhammad, fourth caliph in Sunni reckoning and first Imam of Shiʿi Islam, assassinated at Kufa in 661.  Prophets & Biblical Figures

title: Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī
summary: The martyr of Karbala. Grandson of Muhammad, killed with his companions at Karbala in 680. His death is mourned each year on the day of Ashura.
text: Grandson of Muhammad, killed with his companions at Karbala in 680. His death is mourned each year on the day of Ashura.  Prophets & Biblical Figures
